clue.text: Entertainer has to wriggle about with the sinuous harem queen

parts.note: to snake is to wriggle or wind along
C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: sinuous means twisting and winding, so the letters of harem writhe into a new order

parts.note: R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A performer wriggles about alongside a sultry, swaying queen of the harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinuous' rearranges HAREM into HARME, which sits between C and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake charmer is a street performer who seems to make a snake dance to a pipe.

clue.text: Ticks imperfect goods

explanation.surface: Something ticks off flawed merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick of the clock is a very short moment, as are seconds; seconds are also factory rejects sold cheaply.

clue.text: Bolt that is part of a fastening

annotationWithheld.why: Bolt that is part of a fastening (7) for ABSCOND: no wordplay found; 'Bolt' defines, but nothing in 'that is part of a fastening' builds the letters, and the bolt of a fastening is not the sense the answer takes
annotationWithheld.clue: Bolt that is part of a fastening

clue.text: The boys are of an age

parts.note: Edward is a boy's name
Ian is a second boy's name

explanation.surface: Two lads turn out to be the same age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boys' gives two names, one after the other; 'of an age' is the definition, meaning belonging to a particular era.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwardian describes the period of King Edward VII's reign, 1901-1910, so it belongs to one historical era.

clue.text: Large beast in the shippon

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie within the words the shippon, running across them

explanation.surface: A big animal is kept in the cowshed.
explanation.walkthrough: A shippon is an old dialect word for a cattle shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is a huge African river mammal, a classic large beast.

clue.text: Soldier in uniform

explanation.surface: A soldier dressed in his uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional full-time soldier; regular also means even and consistent, like something uniform.

clue.text: A name in English dance set-up to enthral

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for name within the turned-round English dance
in a down clue set-up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: valse is the French word for waltz, used in English too

explanation.surface: Someone in an English dance troupe is set up to captivate the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns E plus VALSE into ESLAVE; 'in' then places N after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral originally meant to make someone a thrall, a slave, the same idea as making them a captive.

clue.text: Plan Queen Elizabeth imposed on the Commons for a monastery

indicators.note: imposed on means placed on top of, which in a down clue means written above

parts.note: a chart is a map or plan
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth
the House of Commons is called simply the House

explanation.surface: The Queen forces a scheme on the House of Commons concerning a religious house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Charterhouse is a former Carthusian monastery in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A charterhouse is a Carthusian religious community, the Carthusian order's name for a monastery.

clue.text: Chop was rejected by cutter

parts.note: to hack is to chop roughly

indicators.note: rejected suggests something turned back, so the word was is read backwards

explanation.surface: A chopping blow was turned down by the woodcutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting metal, a cutting tool.

clue.text: An example of Medusan bloodstock

parts.note: bloodstock usually means thoroughbred horses; here it is a horse that literally sprang from the blood of the Gorgon Medusa when Perseus beheaded her

explanation.surface: A pedigree horse from the stud of someone called Medusa.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the winged horse Pegasus was born from the blood of the slain Gorgon, Medusa.

clue.text: Servant uses books to press flower

indicators.note: to press means to sit on top of, as books do on flowers; in a down clue that puts one piece above the other

parts.note: Samuel is the name of two books of the Old Testament, First and Second Samuel
read as flow-er, something that flows; a weller is something that wells up

explanation.surface: A domestic uses heavy books to press a flower flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, not a bloom. Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Weller is the cheerful manservant of Mr Pickwick in Dickens's first novel.

clue.text: Spitefulness in Capek's play about a serjeant?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the play's title surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots) is Karel Capek's play that introduced the word robot
a serjeant is a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: A Czech play about an army sergeant is full of malice.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. is the 1920 Czech play that gave English the word robot; 'about' puts A NCO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-lasting resentment, close to spite.

clue.text: The tree that can corrupt?

parts.note: to oil someone's palm, or grease it, is to bribe them, so this tree's name reads as an act of corruption

explanation.surface: A tree with the power to deprave.
explanation.definitionFit: The oil palm is a tropical tree grown for palm oil; its two words reversed describe bribery.

clue.text: A seed perhaps is less under pressure

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of a seed could be something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: A seed may perhaps be under less stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased describes tension relieved or loosened, so less strained.

clue.text: Poke one's nose in hamper

explanation.surface: Someone sticks their nose into a picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to meddle, or to obstruct and hinder something.

clue.text: Choir tend to become elegiac

indicators.note: to become signals that the letters change into something new

explanation.surface: A choir tends to turn mournful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' rearranges CHOIR and TEND together.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament for the dead, so threnodic means mournful like an elegy.

clue.text: Spearman *- the destroyer of Wales according to the saying

definitions.text: the destroyer of Wales according to the saying

explanation.surface: A spear-carrier is said to be the ruin of the Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to the saying' means as spoken: Wales sounds like whales, which a harpoon-thrower kills.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpooner throws a harpoon, a barbed spear, at whales to kill them.

clue.text: Hearing for the second time about the Test

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Someone hears again about the Test match.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrial is a new court hearing of a case already heard once.

clue.text: No cigar can be vital

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of no cigar may become another word

explanation.surface: Giving up cigars can be vital for your health.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic can mean fundamental or essential to the whole, like a living organ.

clue.text: Parrot's bill is part of the mouth

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the bird alone

indicators.note: is part of means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a maw is an animal's mouth or jaws
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A parrot's beak forms part of its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like the parrot's beak, but it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured tropical American parrot.

clue.text: Cosmetic not needed when Susan came aboard

definitions.text: Cosmetic not needed when Susan came aboard

parts.words: Cosmetic not needed when Susan came aboard
parts.note: the old song begins with black-eyed Susan coming aboard, and eyes already black need no darkening make-up

explanation.surface: A woman boards a ship without bothering about her make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The ballad Black-Eyed Susan opens with the fleet moored in the Downs when Susan came aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is the cosmetic used to darken eyelashes.

clue.text: It sounds like a morning train

definitions.text: It sounds like a morning train

parts.words: It sounds like a morning train
parts.note: morning sounds like mourning, and a mourning train is a slow procession behind a hearse

explanation.surface: Something that seems to be an early commuter train.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a funeral procession following the coffin.

clue.text: Uneasy? Get out of bed fast

parts.note: to be up is to be out of bed
fast, as in held fast, means tight

explanation.surface: Feeling restless? Leap out of bed quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like quickly, but it means firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is informal for tense and anxious.

clue.text: A possessive eccentric, Reith

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of Reith go astray

explanation.surface: Lord Reith, the BBC's founder, was a possessive eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges REITH; Lord Reith was the first head of the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is a possessive pronoun or determiner, meaning belonging to them.

clue.text: In Latin we mostly sing the organ part

parts.note: nos is the Latin for we

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to trill is to sing with a warble

explanation.surface: We sing most of the organ part in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final L of TRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the two openings of the nose, the organ of smell.

clue.text: He was on first name terms with Brigadier Gerard

definitions.text: He was on first name terms with Brigadier Gerard

parts.words: He was on first name terms with Brigadier Gerard
parts.note: being on first-name terms usually means friendship; here it is literally the brigadier's own first name

explanation.surface: A close friend of a Napoleonic cavalry officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Brigadier Etienne Gerard is the boastful French hussar of Arthur Conan Doyle's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's Brigadier Gerard has the given name Etienne.

clue.text: Cold look from expert shot in America

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter in the US gives a chilly stare.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead eye is an expressionless stare; a deadeye is American slang for a crack marksman.

clue.text: Animal with power to outrun its pursuers

definitions.text: Animal with power to outrun its pursuers

parts.words: Animal with power to outrun its pursuers
parts.note: the animal is a mechanical lure run on a powered rail, which greyhounds chase but never catch

explanation.surface: A creature strong enough to escape anything hunting it.
explanation.walkthrough: In greyhound racing the dogs chase a lure running on a powered rail round the track.
explanation.definitionFit: The electric hare is the mechanical lure that greyhounds chase round a racetrack.
